nodes.summary: If $p$ is a prime number, then the closure of $\{p\}$ in the positive integers with Macías's coprime topology is the set of positive integers divisible by $p$.
nodes.title: Closure of a prime in Macías's coprime topology

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$, $\Omega_n$ is the set of positive integers $m$ with $\gcd(n, m) = 1$.
nodes.title: Positive integers coprime to a given integer

nodes.summary: Equip the positive integers with the comaximal topology, the topology generated by the sets $\{m : \gcd(n, m) = 1\}$ for positive integers $n$. If $a$ and $b$ are coprime positive integers, then the arithmetic progression $\{ak + b : k \in \mathbb{N}\} = \{b, a + b, 2a + b, \dots\}$, with $k$ ranging over the natural numbers including $0$, is dense in this topology.
nodes.title: Coprime arithmetic progressions are dense in the comaximal space

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be the positive integers with Macías's coprime topology and $X_1$ the subspace of positive integers different from $1$. If the set of prime numbers is dense in $X_1$, then it is dense in $X$.
nodes.title: Density of the primes passes from the subspace without 1

nodes.summary: The set of prime numbers is dense in the set of positive integers different from $1$, with the subspace topology induced by Macías's coprime topology on the positive integers.
nodes.title: The primes are dense in the coprime topology without 1

nodes.summary: Equip the positive integers with the comaximal topology, the topology generated by the sets $\{m : \gcd(n, m) = 1\}$ for positive integers $n$. A nonempty set $A$ of primes is infinite if and only if it is dense in this topology.
nodes.title: A nonempty set of primes is dense in the comaximal space iff it is infinite

nodes.summary: There are infinitely many prime numbers if and only if the set of prime numbers is dense in the positive integers with Macías's coprime topology.
nodes.title: Infinitude of the primes as density

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ let $\Omega_n$ be the set of positive integers coprime to $n$. The family $\beta = \{\Omega_n : n \ge 1\}$ is a basis of the topology on the positive integers that it generates (Macías's coprime topology).
nodes.title: Macías's coprime sets form a basis

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ let $\Omega_n$ be the set of positive integers coprime to $n$. Macías's coprime basis is the family $\beta = \{\Omega_n : n \ge 1\}$ of subsets of the positive integers.
nodes.title: Macías's coprime basis

nodes.summary: The topology $\tau_1$ on the set of positive integers different from $1$ is the subspace topology induced by Macías's coprime topology $\tau$ on the positive integers.
nodes.title: Macías's coprime topology without 1

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ let $\Omega_n$ be the set of positive integers coprime to $n$. Macías's coprime topology $\tau$ is the topology on the positive integers generated by the sets $\Omega_n$, $n \ge 1$, that is, the coarsest topology in which every $\Omega_n$ is open.
nodes.title: Macías's coprime topology

nodes.summary: Within the set of positive integers different from $1$, this is the subset consisting of the prime numbers.
nodes.title: Primes among the positive integers different from 1

nodes.summary: The set of positive integers that are prime numbers.
nodes.title: Primes among the positive integers

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
